propositions: A single mapped project's transport failure (400/401/403/404/429/5xx/timeout) in base-query iteration aborts the entire reconciler pass for all projects due to lack of per-project error isolation.

The enrichment loop already implements fail-open per-project resilience, but the base-query loop does not, creating asymmetric vulnerability where a nonexistent project key (syntactically valid but unknown to Jira) terminates the whole pass.

Extracted _fetch_project helper must drain both active and done-recent queries into a local dict and merge atomically into the shared snapshot only on success, ensuring no partial keys from a failed project leak into snapshot as false deletions.

Per-project transport errors emit fetcher-project-fetch-failed alerts and continue to other projects; syntactically-invalid keys still fail closed outside the try block; BackendPaginationStallError still re-raises to surface truncation.
